To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DL algorithms are able to predict driver's drowsiness and alertness states with high accuracy and the proposed methods outperform the conventional DL solutions as well as other state-of-the-art algorithms.
CCNN and its variation (CCNN-R) outperform other DL methods for prediction of cognitive states from EEG.

CCNN and its variant CCNN-R achieve the best performance for cross-session prediction of driver's drowziness and alertness states from EEG signals, and the DL methods with raw EEG inputs achieve better performance than the ICA features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of cognitive states of the driver from EEG signals.
the prediction of driver's fatigue using EEG data with DL methods.
the development of novel DL-based algorithms for prediction of cognitive states using EEG signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCNN-R is the best DL method for cross-session predictions of driver's cognitive state using EEG.
DL methods are promising for driver's fatigue detection, but more work is needed to improve performance.
the DL solutions are promising for driver's fatigue detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed CCNN and CC NN-R algorithms can achieve better performance than the conventional DL methods and other non-DL solutions for the prediction of drowsy and awake states.
CCNN and its variations are more effective than other DL methods for EEG-based driver's drowsiness prediction and DL methods are better than other machine learning techniques.
DL solutions outperform the non-DL methods, CCNN and CC-NN-R are superior to DNN and CNN and the DL solutions using raw EEG inputs outperform those using ICA features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCNN and its variant CCNN-R are promising DL solutions for EEG-based cognitive state prediction.
the DL methods can be used for cross-session predictions of driver's cognitive state with high accuracy.
the DL solutions can be successfully used for prediction of driver fatigue from EEG data.
